title: Covered Days When Several Proofs or a Short Proof Reach the Period — Collateral Protection Insurance Closing-Period Refund
content:
For the closing-period refund under Collateral Protection Insurance, the covered days of the refunded charge's period are set by the number of accepted proofs that reach the covered stretch and, for a single reaching proof, by whether it expires inside the period.

A proof reaches the covered stretch when its expiration date falls on or after the period start and it took effect on or before the closed date; its span runs from the later of the period start and its effective date through the earlier of its expiration date and the closed date.

| Reaching proofs | Covered days |
|---|---|
| two or more | the days inside any of their spans, a day inside several counted once |
| exactly one, expiring inside the period | the days of its span |
| any other case (exactly one, not expiring inside the period) | the days of the period from the latest policy effective date among the reaching proofs through the closed date, both ends counted |

## Hypothetical spans

Days are numbered within a hypothetical period:

- Two reaching proofs with spans day 1 to day 12 and day 18 to day 30: covered days are 12 and 13, that is 25.
- Two reaching proofs with spans day 1 to day 20 and day 15 to day 30: days 15 to 20 lie inside both and count once, so the covered days are the 30 days from day 1 to day 30.
- One reaching proof, effective day 5 and expiring on day 16 of the period: covered days are its span, day 5 to day 16, that is 12.
